data.narrative:
PLD Space is a Series G-stage space and aerospace company that has raised €120M to date across its financing history. The valuation landscape for this sector includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers, though direct comparable transactions at the same stage remain sparse.

The stage-progression method is the sole applicable triangulation approach for this valuation. Using total capital raised (€120M, approximately $209M) as a base proxy and applying a typical Series G to subsequent-stage step-up multiplier of 1.25x yields an implied valuation of $261M. Public market anchoring, while informative—the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 25.3x revenue across six public names—cannot be operationalized without PLD Space's disclosed revenue figure, which is not on file. Peer-median triangulation was similarly inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting statistical thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $222M (low) to $300M (high), with a median point of $261M. This estimate carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single methodology. Key dependencies include the accuracy of the stage-progression multiplier as applied to early-stage aerospace capital deployed, and the absence of revenue visibility that would allow validation through public market multiples. Resolution of revenue disclosure or identification of more proximate private transactions would strengthen conviction in this range.
